question: Refeeding syndrome in a severely malnourished anorexia nervosa patient is primarily caused by a precipitous fall in serum phosphate after reintroduction of carbohydrate-containing feeds.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is true. Refeeding syndrome results from the rapid intracellular shift of electrolytes — especially phosphate — driven by insulin release when carbohydrate feeding is restarted in a chronically malnourished patient. The fall in serum phosphate is the central mechanism. The clinical solution is to start nutritional rehabilitation slowly and monitor serum phosphate daily.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. Carbohydrate feeding triggers insulin release, which drives phosphate, potassium, and magnesium from the serum into cells. Hypophosphataemia is the hallmark biochemical finding in refeeding syndrome and can cause cardiac arrhythmias, respiratory failure, rhabdomyolysis, and seizures. Start feeds at low caloric density and monitor electrolytes closely.
